communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA US Army record 8/6
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Military service records concerning below:
Name: Harrison Reves 
Branch: United States Army
DOB: 12/13/1946 
Dates of Service: Approx yrs 1965 to 1985

Please provide the following documents 
1. copy of Bronze Star Medal award citation 
2. copy of Army commendation award citations
3. copy of Meritorious Service Medal citation 
4. copy of Army Achievement medal citation 
5. Section II Military Education/ training courses form
6. Section V MISCELLANEOUS Form
7. Dates of service, date of discharge from active duty 
8. Historical Assignments

I request hard copies of paperwork in the file showing this information. Please redact per U.S.C. § 552(b)(6).
Please mail hardcopies to following:
MUCKROCK NEWS 
DEPT MR#
263 HUNTINGTON AVE
BOSTON, MA 02115

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Eric Bradley

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: CIA MDR
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Mandatory Declassification Review request: withheld portions of five released STARGATE (CREST) documents, 1974-1976

Dear Information and Privacy Coordinator,

Under Section 3.5 of Executive Order 13526, I request mandatory declassification review of the withheld portions of the following documents, which the Agency has already released in its STARGATE collection (CREST). Each is identified by its CREST document number, so it can be located with little effort. To my knowledge none is the subject of pending litigation, and none has been reviewed for declassification in the past two years.

1. CIA-RDP79-00999A000300100011-9, OTS/CB memorandum of 21 January 1975, page 3, paragraph 7: the redacted name of the test "given ... by OTS/BAB" to P. Price and H. Hammid.

2. CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050001-5, "Paranormal Investigations: Outline of 'Basic' Research Tasks": on the first page, the redaction in the line "WAIS/PAS test (by ...)" and the withheld handwritten annotations; on the last page, the redactions in paragraph 9 of Part IV.

3. CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050006-0, OTS/BAB Memorandum 163-75, 29 April 1975: the two pages marked "Next 2 Page(s) In Document Exempt," and the redacted block following "Coordinates given Pat:" on page 2 of the memorandum for the record.

4. CIA-RDP96-00787R000700100003-3, SRI Proposal ISH 74-266, 20 December 1974: the page marked "PAGE(S) 7 MISSING," and the four pages marked "Next 4 Page(s) In Document Exempt" that precede Dr. H. E. Puthoff's letter of 12 July 1974.

5. CIA-RDP96-00787R000200120001-8, letter of 26 February 1976 from Dr. H. E. Puthoff: the redacted addressee block.

Basis. Items 1 through 4 date from 1974 and 1975 and are now more than 50 years old. Under Section 3.3(h) of Executive Order 13526, classified information that old is declassified unless its release should clearly and demonstrably be expected to reveal the identity of a confidential human source or a human intelligence source, or key design concepts of weapons of mass destruction, or unless it falls within an exemption approved under Section 3.3(h)(2). The name of a psychological test, the office that administered it, and the contents of a 1974 proposal for medical and psychological testing are none of these. The redactions in these documents were made when they were released between 2001 and 2003, well before the 50-year mark. Item 5 (February 1976) reaches 50 years on 31 December 2026; I ask that it be reviewed under the standard that applies on the date of review.

Where a personal name must remain withheld on another legal basis, I ask that the office or component be released in its place. If any portion remains classified, I ask that the response identify the specific exemption category relied on for each withheld portion, so that I can consider an appeal.

I am a researcher and author and will publish the results. Electronic copies, please.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: CIA MKULTRA
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. These documents, which appear by number in the index the Agency supplied with its 2004 MKULTRA CD-ROM release (request F-2004-01329) but were not included on the CD-ROMs or in the October 2018 supplemental release:
   a. document 21994, 3 April 1972, "Comments (with attached article)";
   b. document 21995, 9 July 1971, "Behavioral Activities";
   c. document 21999, 26 July 1973, "Divisional Review ... Behavioral Activities/Behavioral Systems/Animal";
   d. document 22000, 21 July 1972, receipts of unclassified publications;
   e. document 163363, June 1972, one page, indexed as "Travel for [deleted]".

2. Any Agency response to, or evaluation of, the June 1972 EG&G Albuquerque Division "Unsolicited Proposal for Research in Monitoring Living Plants" (AL-P-72-73), which the Agency released in the same MKULTRA collection.

If any of the item 1 documents was reviewed and withheld in full in an earlier release, please say so and identify the exemption, so that I can decide whether to seek review.

Search. These records come from the files of the Agency's MKULTRA-era behavioral research, which was the specific subject of congressional investigation in 1977 (including the joint hearing of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and the Subcommittee on Health and Scientific Research, 3 August 1977). Under 50 U.S.C. 3141(c), files concerning the specific subject matter of such an investigation remain subject to search and review.

Segregation. Please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions.

Format. Electronic copies, please.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

for 1 January 1973 through 31 December 1977. Items 1 through 5 are cited by originator, subject and date in an Agency publication, Kenneth A. Kress, "Parapsychology in Intelligence: A Personal Review and Conclusions," Studies in Intelligence, Vol. 21, No. 4 (Winter 1977), released by the Agency as CIA-RDP96-00791R000200030040-0 ("Kress 1977").

1. Kress 1977, footnote 17: OTS/SDB, Notes on Interviews with F. P., E. L., C. J., K. G., and V. C., January 1975 (SECRET).

2. Kress 1977, footnote 18: DDO/NE, Memorandum for OTS/BAB, Subject: Experimental Collection Activity Relating to Libya, 8 October 1975 (SECRET), with its attachments.

3. Kress 1977, footnote 16:
   a. Chief/Division D/DDO, Memorandum for C/D&E, Subject: Perceptual Augmentation Techniques, 24 January 1975;
   b. AC/SE/DDO, Memorandum for C/D&E, Subject: Perceptual Augmentation Testing, 14 January 1975;
   c. C/EA/DDO, Memorandum for Director of Technical Service, Subject: Exploration of Operational Potential of "Paranormals", 5 February 1975;
   d. C/Libya/EL/NE/DDO, Memorandum for OTS/CB, Subject: Libyan Desk Requirement for Psychic Experiments Relating to Libya, 31 January 1975;
   e. CI/Staff/DDO, Memorandum for the Record, Subject: SRI Experiment, 12 December 1974.

4. Kress 1977, footnote 15: C/AOB/OTS, Memorandum for the Record, Subject: Parapsychology/"Remote Viewing", 20 April 1976 (printed as "S/AOB/OTS" in the 1999 reprint of the article, Journal of Scientific Exploration, Vol. 13, No. 1). Kress cites this memorandum for the operations officer's conclusion on Mr. Price's remote viewing of two foreign embassies, "It is my considered opinion that this technique ... offers definite operational possibilities." I also request any other written evaluation of that test by the operations officer, which Kress's 1999 Postscript describes as "a written, positive evaluation."

5. These records, also cited in Kress 1977, which I have not found in the Agency's STARGATE release:
   a. footnote 7: K. Green, LSD/OSI, Memorandum for the Record, Subject: Verification of Remote Viewing Experiments at Stanford Research Institute, 9 November 1973;
   b. footnote 10: S. L. Cianci, LSR/ORD, Memorandum for OTS/CB, Subject: Response to Requested Critique, SRI Random Stimulus Generator Results, 12 June 1975;
   c. footnote 12: W. T. Strand, C/ESO/IAS, Memorandum for Director, Office of Technical Service, Subject: Evaluation of Data on Semipalatinsk Unidentified R&D Facility No. 3, USSR, 20 August 1974.

6. Reports and evaluations of the "Operational tests which continued after SRI funding stopped," as described in OTS/CB Memorandum 76-86 of 4 May 1976 (CIA-RDP79-00999A000300100005-6), for 1975 through 1977, including the evaluation by the requesting area desk described as a "somewhat confusing, but nevertheless official, report" (September 1975) in the Agency's outline of its ESP research (CIA-RDP79-00999A000400050014-1).

7. The two attachments listed on OTS/CB Memorandum 76-86 ("CIA Visit Request" and "Attendees").

8. Records of the receipt, evaluation and disposition of two Stanford Research Institute proposals, including any reply to Dr. H. E. Puthoff:
   a. Proposal ISH 74-266, "Technical Services," 20 December 1974 (CIA-RDP96-00787R000700100003-3);
   b. Proposal ISH 76-68, "Detection of Remote Low-Level EM Sources," 1 March 1976 (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200120002-7), with its cover letter of 26 February 1976 (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200120001-8).

Search. The Directorate of Operations memoranda in items 2 and 3 were addressed to Office of Technical Service components (OTS/BAB, OTS/CB and the Director of Technical Service, among others), and all of items 1 through 5 were available to the author of an Agency journal article in 1977. Copies therefore exist outside the originating Directorate of Operations files. Under 50 U.S.C. 3141(d), information disseminated from operational files into non-exempt files remains subject to search and review, even if the originating file is exempt. I ask that those locations be searched: the Office of Technical Service (including OTS/SDB, OTS/CB, OTS/BAB and OTS/AOB), the Office of Research and Development, and the files from which the Agency released its STARGATE collection in 2000 to 2004.

Retired records. In July 1986 the Office of Research and Development told SRI International that the primary data from the Price experiments (transcripts, drawings and audio tapes) were no longer available to the writer, that he could not determine "if these data were destroyed or if they reside somewhere in archives," and that he was declining further efforts to locate them (CIA-RDP96-00787R000200020041-5; see also CIA-RDP96-00787R000200020040-6). No search was made then. I ask that this search include retired and archived Office of Technical Service and Office of Research and Development records.

Privacy. I do not seek the names of individuals and accept their redaction.

Segregation. Please release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. If a record is withheld in full, please identify it and the exemption claimed.

Format and timing. I ask for electronic copies, and for interim releases as records are processed.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure
